item.title: Fly-tipping Fines Set To Rise To £1,000 Across Harborough
item.description: Harborough District Council is set to increase the maximum fine for fly-tipping from £400 to £1,000 as part wider measures to deal with the issue. Extra resources are also planned to speed-up investigations and remove illegally dumped waste more quickly, while working more closely with the police and Environment Agency. item.description: East Midlands Railway has reinstated a late night weekday train from London to Market Harborough after several years. item.title: Santa Motorcyclists Stage Charity Ride Out
item.description: Motorcyclists dressed as Santa have taken part in a festive fundraising ride-out in and around Market Harborough. The convoy of over 20 decorated bikes gathered on The Square during yesterday’s event, which raised £240 for Leicestershire and Rutland Blood Bikes. item.title: Bus Strikes Averted After Pay Deal Accepted
item.description: Arriva bus workers in Leicestershire have accepted new pay deal meaning strike action has been averted. The Unite union had paused planned industrial action while the new offer was considered by drivers, depot and office staff. item.title: Emergency Services Respond To Crash On B6047
item.description: Nobody was seriously injured after a two vehicle crash on the B6047 near Church Langton. Emergency services were called just after 1.15pm today and Melton Road was temporarily closed while the incident was dealt with. Police, East Midlands Ambulance Service and fire crews from Market Harborough and Kibworth attended the scene.

item.title: HDC Begins Investigating Town Council Option
item.description: Harborough District Council has started the process of exploring whether Market Harborough should have its own town council. The move follows a petition signed by more than 1,800 residents and was formally agreed by councillors at a meeting last night. item.title: Illuminated Sculpture Planned For Friendship Park
item.description: Plans have been unveiled for a new illuminated sculpture at Market Harborough’s Friendship Park.
